hypotheses.justification: The statement doesn't need it. `cohomFpMap` (ContCohomology/TrivialFp.lean, variables `(p : ℕ) {G H K}` with group/topology instances only) and `absoluteGaloisGroupProPQuotientMap` (AbsoluteGaloisGroup/ProP.lean, variables `(p : ℕ) (K) [Field K]`) take no primality assumption. The binder is only an argument because it is an instance variable in scope. The proof doesn't need it either. It calls `inflH2MaximalProP_injective`, which takes `[Fact p.Prime]` only from its `variable` line; its proof never uses it. That proof uses `trivialZModAction`, `zmodEquivFixedPointsOfTrivialAction` and `cohomFpAddEquivH2` (TrivialFp/Explicit.lean, variables without Fact), `explicitMap2Equiv`, `cohomFpAddEquivH2_cohomFpMap_quotientMk_eq_explicitInfl2` (TrivialFp/Inflation.lean, variables `(p : ℕ) (G) ... [CompactSpace G]`, no Fact) and `explicitInfl2_proPKernel_injective`. The last one is stated in a section with `{p : ℕ}` and no Fact, so its dependency `subsingleton_h1ConjInvariants_proPKernel` cannot need primality either. Its hypothesis `p • m = 0` on `ZMod p` comes from `nsmul_eq_mul, ZMod.natCast_self`, which holds for every p. So the same proof works for any natural number p, including 0, 1 and composites. The fix is to copy that proof with `omit [Fact p.Prime]` and apply it to `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K`, which is a compact, totally disconnected topological group. This was not compiled. A small remaining risk is that instance search inside that proof silently routes through the prime instance, which is unlikely since every lemma it calls is stated without one.
